proposal: The Mandate recommends that USDA counter scare tactics about agricultural biotechnology and adopt policies removing unnecessary barriers to approvals and adoption. It also recommends working with Congress to repeal the 2016 federal bioengineered food labeling law while keeping federal preemption and stressing that voluntary labeling is allowed, and using all tools, with the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative, against foreign barriers such as Mexico's planned ban on genetically modified yellow corn.

status_summary: On approvals, APHIS stopped preparing National Environmental Policy Act analyses for reviews of petitions for nonregulated status as of 2025-07-09 and withdrew two pending environmental impact statement notices on 2025-08-18, one of which concerned a maize later deregulated on 2026-08-05; USDA also published a request for information on 2026-05-15 on potential risk-based deregulation of modified organisms, with a deregulatory rule listed on the regulatory agenda but not published. APHIS separately restored its pre-2020 biotechnology rules on 2025-06-16 to reflect a December 2024 court vacatur of the 2020 rule. On trade, USDA said on 2025-02-06 that it welcomed Mexico's withdrawal of the GE corn measures challenged under USMCA and would work with USTR to monitor compliance; Mexico amended its constitution on 2025-03-17 to bar planting of GE corn, and no formal US response to that step was found. On labeling, no repeal bill or USDA request for repeal was found; in Natural Grocers v. Rollins a federal court on 2026-08-03 ordered three provisions of the disclosure rule vacated effective 2028-01-01. The stage reflects the operative streamlining of approvals only.

timeline.event: USDA stated it applauded Mexico for declaring ineffective the genetically engineered corn measures challenged under USMCA, and said it would work with USTR to monitor compliance.
Mexico issued a decree amending its Constitution so that corn grown in Mexico must be free of genetic modification, which bars planting GE corn without expressly addressing imports.
APHIS published a final rule restoring its pre-2020 biotechnology regulations in the Code of Federal Regulations to match the December 2024 court vacatur of the 2020 rule.

APHIS published a notice withdrawing two notices of intent to prepare environmental impact statements, stating that since a 2025-07-09 program update it no longer prepares NEPA analyses for reviews of petitions for nonregulated status.
A CRS report said APHIS was operating under the pre-2020 rules and that an interim final rule on exemptions and simplified procedures was listed on the regulatory agenda but unpublished.
USDA published a request for information on regulating modified organisms under the Plant Protection Act, with comments due 2026-06-15.
USDA extended the comment period on the modified organisms request for information to 2026-06-30.

In Natural Grocers v. Rollins, the Northern District of California ordered vacatur, effective 2028-01-01, of three provisions of the bioengineered food disclosure rule (the detectability exclusion and the QR code and text message options), denying USDA's request for a 2029 date.
APHIS announced that MON 87429 maize, one of the two petitions whose environmental impact statements were withdrawn, is no longer regulated.

title: Counter biotech opposition, repeal federal bioengineered labeling, press trade barriers
uncertainties: No bill repealing the National Bioengineered Food Disclosure Standard was found by the researcher, and no USDA statement seeking repeal was found; the review did not search further. The 2026-08-03 order is known from a law-firm alert dated 2026-08-26; the order itself was not read. The 2026 Unified Agenda lists a disclosure rulemaking tied to the court remand, read only as an API abstract. The Mexico amendment details come from a law-firm article dated 2025-04-04, which mentions a USDA attache report calling its scope ambiguous; a formal US response after 2025-03-17 and the 2026 USMCA review's treatment of biotech were not found. The CRS biotechnology report links a 2025-10-31 Ninth Circuit opinion (case 22-16770); that case number matches the labeling litigation rather than the 2020 rule vacatur, which the Federal Register dates to 2024-12-02 in National Family Farm Coalition v. Vilsack. The interim final rule titled Regaining Lost Efficiencies for Products of Biotechnology appears only as a CRS account of a regulatory agenda entry. The NEPA change follows a USDA-wide July 2025 revision of its NEPA rules rather than a biotech-specific policy. EPA, FDA and Make America Healthy Again report positions on biotechnology were not researched.
